title: 唐會要 99, 拂菻國 — the Tang institutional record of Fulin: four hundred walled cities, twelve joint ministers, a striking water-clock, and the embassy of Zhenguan 17 (643)
language_note: Literary Chinese, in the register prose of a Song institutional compendium — a 會要, built from Tang court archives and organised by institution rather than by reign. The genre is the point: this is not narrative and not ethnography but an administrative dossier on a foreign state, which is the class of text FINDING 45 identified as untranslated. 拂菻 is the Tang transcription for Byzantium and the excerpt's own first clause supplies the equation with the Han-era 大秦. NOTE THE GLASS GRAPH: this text writes 頗璃 where eastasia-06-cefu-yuangui writes 頗黎, for the same substance in the same embassy.
date: Compiled 961 CE, from Tang court archives. The excerpt's datable notices run from Zhenguan 17 (643) to Kaiyuan 10 (722) and reach back to Sui Yangdi (r. 604-618). UNLIKE eastasia-06, THE ERA NAMES ARE IN THE EXCERPT — 貞觀十七年, 乾封元年, 開元十年 are all present in its own verbatim text, so the record dates itself without reaching back to an entry it did not capture. One era name in the excerpt, 大定, is not a Tang era; see original_text_note, where it is recorded and NOT resolved.
original_text_excerpt: 拂菻國一名大秦在西海之國北東南與波斯接地方萬里列城四百邑居連屬其宫室柱梲多以水晶琉璃為之有貴臣十二共理國正事常使一人將嚢随王車百姓有事者即以事投嚢中王至宫省發理其枉直其王無常人簡賢者立之國有災異及風雨不時即廢之有鳥似鶴其毛綠色常在王邊倚枕上坐每進食有毒其烏輒鳴户十萬餘南臨大海城東面有一大門髙二十丈飾以黄金凡有大門三重第二大門之樓懸一金秤以金丸十二枚係于衡端以候日之十二時焉為一金人其大如人立於側毎至一時其金丸輒落鏗然發聲金人即應聲引唱以紀日時毫釐無差其殿以瑟瑟為柱黄金為地象牙為門扇香木為棟梁無瓦以白石末塗屋上如玉石焉盛夏之時引水潜上屋四簷飛溜激氣成凉風有羊生于土中其國人候其欲萌乃築墻以院之防外獸所食然其臍與地連割之則死惟人著甲走馬及擊銅鼓以駭之其羊驚鳴而臍絶便逐水草諸珍寳多出其國隋焬帝常欲通之竟不能致貞觀十七年其王波多力遣使獻赤頗璃石綠金精等物後臣大食國乾封元年遣使獻底陀伽大定二年復遣使朝貢開元十年正月遣吐火羅大首領獻獅子二羚羊二四月又遣大徳僧来朝
original_text_note:
Verbatim Literary Chinese, 429 characters in 22 columns, COPIED BY HAND from Kanripo raw.githubusercontent.com/kanripo/KR2m0002/master/KR2m0002_099.txt on 2026-09-04, spanning <pb:KR2m0002_WYG_099-24a> through <pb:KR2m0002_WYG_099-25a>.

EDITORIAL ACTS, DECLARED. Kanripo's ¶ line markers and its <pb:...> page markers are removed and the words they split are closed up — one word is split, 輒|鳴 at the 24a/24b boundary. The lemma heading's two leading ideographic spaces, which are the recension's indent, are removed; the heading 拂菻國 itself is KEPT, because it is what makes the excerpt self-identifying and because the record would otherwise open on a pronoun-less clause naming Da Qin. No punctuation is added; the source carries none.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE BLIND PASTE MADE TO THE LOCATING FETCH, recorded because they are the reason the capture rule exists. FIRST, the locating fetch placed the lemma's start at page 24b. The heading is on 24a, two columns after that page marker, and the curator's paste is what showed it. SECOND, the locating fetch reported the lemma at 'about 1,200' and 'about 1,388 characters'. It is 429. 429 characters is 1,287 bytes in UTF-8, and with the ¶ and <pb:...> markers the span is about 1,388 BYTES — SO THE FIGURE WAS MEASURED IN BYTES AND REPORTED IN CHARACTERS. A Literary Chinese character is three bytes, so the error is threefold and it runs in the direction that makes a passage look more substantial than it is. Neither correction was available to any amount of re-fetching; both came out of a human reading the page.

THE CAPTURE WAS REPEATED AND THE REPETITION AGREES. The curator pasted the six columns on 24a twice, in two separate messages, and the two pastes are byte-identical at 126 characters. This is the first record in this corpus whose capture was checked against anything other than itself, and it is checkable at all because the text has TWO open witnesses — Kanripo KR2m0002 and zh.wikisource.org/wiki/唐會要/卷099 — where every other Literary Chinese record in this corpus has one.

THE RECENSION IS THE WENYUANGE SIKU QUANSHU and the page marker says so — WYG. The third record in this corpus to confirm F4_CANDIDATES' warning against Kanripo's base edition from its own file rather than on the hunt document's authority. The orthography shows it: 髙 for 高, 毎 for 每, 焬 for 煬. The Qianlong editors are known to have altered passages about foreign peoples and this is a dossier on a foreign people. AND THE FILE CARRIES AT LEAST ONE PLAIN GRAPHIC ERROR IN ADJACENT MATTER: the 流鬼國 lemma two entries earlier reads 貝觀十四年 for 貞觀十四年. That is outside the excerpt and it is recorded because a recension with a visible error two entries away is not a recension whose cleanliness may be assumed.

ONE ERA NAME IS RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED. The excerpt reads 大定二年 between 乾封元年 (666) and 開元十年 (722). 大定 is not a Tang era. This record does NOT adjudicate what it should read: no collation against a Zhonghua Shuju edition was performed because none is openly reachable from this project, and a reading this project supplied itself would be worth nothing — FINDING 55, and the same restraint eastasia-05-liangshu-qin-lun exercised over 黝歙. Stated, uncollated, correctable by somebody opening a book.

notes:
F5 Part 2, record 36, and the tranche's one verbatim_machine_english record. It is also the LAST such record this project can curate: FINDING 63 established that F6 and F7 place no vme slot, so this is the whole of the tier's remaining evidence and it is aimed at FINDING 45's named seam.

WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT ROME. A Tang administrative dossier on Byzantium, opening by welding the Han-era name 大秦 to the Tang-era 拂菻 in its first clause. Four hundred walled cities; palace pillars of rock-crystal and glass; twelve senior ministers governing jointly; a bag carried beside the king's carriage into which any subject may throw a petition; a king who is not hereditary but chosen for worth AND DEPOSED WHEN THERE ARE PORTENTS OR UNSEASONABLE WEATHER; a great gate faced with gold; a striking water-clock of twelve golden balls and a golden figure that calls the hours; water drawn up to the eaves in high summer to make a cool wind; and the lamb that grows out of the ground on a navel-cord. Then the notices: the embassy of Zhenguan 17, later subjection to the 大食, and gifts of lions and antelopes in Kaiyuan 10.

THE PARALLEL WITNESS, AND IT DISAGREES — WHICH IS WHY THIS RECORD IS WORTH MORE THAN A SECOND COPY. eastasia-06-cefu-yuangui records the SAME embassy of Zhenguan 17 (643) from the other Song compendium. The two do not agree on what was given. The Cefu Yuangui has 赤頗黎綠頗黎石綠金精 — red glass, GREEN GLASS, malachite, gold-essence. This text has 赤頗璃石綠金精 — red glass, malachite, gold-essence, and NO green glass, with the glass graph written 璃 rather than 黎. Two imperial compilations, fifty-two years apart, both built from Tang court records, differing on an item in a gift list and on how to write the word for glass. The corpus now holds one event in two independent witnesses, and the divergence is recorded here rather than smoothed: neither is corrected against the other, because this project has no reachable collation and a resolution it supplied itself would be worth nothing.

THE ENGLISH SEARCH THAT FAILED, WHICH RULING 57 MAKES PART OF THE TIER. Named sources, not a count, and re-run in F5 rather than inherited from F4. Hirth, China and the Roman Orient (1885) — checked against the book's own table of contents and its lettered source list at pp. 35-36, which enumerate fifteen translated texts; the Tang Huiyao is not among them. Hirth & Rockhill 1911. Yule, Cathay and the Way Thither (1866). Four open sourcebook sites: Fordham's Internet East Asian History Sourcebook — read through its Silk Road Seattle mirror, and it reproduces exactly Hirth's fifteen — Silk Road Seattle, silkroadfoundation.org, silk-road.com. Databases: archive.org full-text search, HathiTrust, Cambridge Core, ScienceDirect, DOAJ, eScholarship, academia.edu, ResearchGate, Google Books, JSTOR open content. chinaknowledge.de's page for the text could not be read at all — it sits in an http/https redirect loop — and that is recorded as unread rather than as negative. THE SHARPEST SINGLE RESULT: archive.org full-text search on "Tang Huiyao" AND "Fulin" returned ZERO results.

THE BOUNDARY, STATED. Print-only monographs were not consulted and one of them matters: Leslie & Gardiner, The Roman Empire in Chinese Sources (Rome, 1996), 422 pages, is the standard translation-corpus of exactly this material and nothing openly reachable establishes whether it covers this lemma. Google Books offers no preview and no snippet view; the Cambridge Core review PDF was refused; the AAR catalogue record refused. The one indirect signal is that Hoppál's open survey of the Chinese Da Qin corpus enumerates the standard texts, cites Leslie & Gardiner as its translation authority, and includes none of the three F5 candidates — suggestive, not decisive. If Leslie & Gardiner covers this entry, this record's tier is wrong and the correction is to name the page. That is ruling 57's difference: the claim is not 'no English translation exists' but 'this curator searched here and found none'.

THE HONEST WEAKNESS, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS THE BOUNDARY. This lemma's descriptive matter runs closely parallel to the Fulin accounts in Jiu Tangshu 198 and Xin Tangshu 221, BOTH OF WHICH HIRTH TRANSLATES and both of which are openly reachable. That is a parallel-witness overlap and not a translation of the Tang Huiyao — a reader can get much of this content in English under another text's name, exactly as F4 recorded for the Lingwai Daida against the Zhufan Zhi. It is stated here because a record whose notes list only what is absent is the document FINDING 47 is about. It is also the reason the Taiping Huanyuji was NOT taken: its overlap is direct quotation of a source Hirth translates in full, where this is two compilations drawing on the same archive.

FINDING 45 IS WHY THIS RECORD EXISTS AND F5's OWN HUNT NARROWED THE CLAIM. The nineteenth-century sinologists translated the dynastic histories and left the huiyao, the leishu and the geographies alone, so the tier is fed by GENRE and genre is something a curator can aim at. F5 aimed at it in two further traditions — Persian and Sanskrit — found the untranslated genre in both, and could fill neither, because the seam is necessary and not sufficient: the tier also needs a machine-readable edition of the untranslated genre, and East Asia has Kanripo where those traditions have photographs of books. See F5_CANDIDATES.md.

RULING 71 AND RULING 72. This record is the subject of both. Ruling 71 predicts it appears in beaten_by for at least one china-describes-rome pair and names its own blind spot in advance — both pairs sit outside the recall window, so a crowder arriving at rank 7 would operate invisibly, and F5_PART2_RESULT reports beaten_by AND rank for both. Ruling 72 predicted this slot would fill and it has. The prediction stays unread until the ranking check runs after this record is in the index.

subject_places.name: Fulin (拂菻), and 大秦 in the text's own first clause
subject_places.note: 拂菻, the Tang name for Byzantium. The excerpt supplies the identification itself — its opening clause gives 一名大秦, 'one name for it is Da Qin' — so the equation is IN the source here rather than imported from the Xin Tangshu as it was for eastasia-06. 大秦 IS NOT PLACED SEPARATELY, and that is a decision rather than an omission: PLACES.md requires every named place to be placed, and 大秦 is not a second place but the same polity under an older name, which the text says in so many words. Ground `regional` with no gazetteer id, as eastasia-01-weilue and eastasia-06 both carry it: a polity, not a settlement, and the whole lemma is organised around it, which makes it the focus.

subject_places.name: the Western Sea (西海)
subject_places.note: The sea the text places Fulin in relation to in its opening clause. Placed because PLACES.md places every named place and a sea is a place — the Periplus records place the Nile on the same rule. Ground `regional` and no id: which body of water a Tang compiler meant by 西海 is exactly the kind of identification this corpus refuses to make on a record's behalf. `mentioned`: nothing moves through it in this passage.

subject_places.name: the great sea to the south (大海)
subject_places.note: Named separately from 西海 in the passage — the text says Fulin looks south onto it — and therefore placed separately, without any claim that the two are or are not the same water. Ground `regional`, no id, for the same reason.

subject_places.name: Persia (波斯)
subject_places.note: Named as bordering Fulin to the south-east. `mentioned` and not a directional role: the text records adjacency, and nothing moves between them in this passage. Ground `regional` and no id — the corpus holds Persia as a region of its own and resolving a Tang exonym to a coordinate would be resolving what the source left as a name.

subject_places.name: the Dashi (大食), the Arabs
subject_places.note: The passage records that Fulin afterwards became subject to them. That is a political relation and not a movement of goods, people or knowledge, so it takes `mentioned` rather than a directional role — the roles vocabulary describes what travels, and subjection does not travel.

subject_places.name: Tokharistan (吐火羅)
subject_places.note: Named in the Kaiyuan 10 (722) notice, where a great chieftain of Tokharistan is dispatched with lions and antelopes. `mentioned` rather than `source` or `waypoint`, and the restraint is deliberate: the movement in that notice runs from Fulin to a court the excerpt never names, so any directional role assigned here would be an edge one of whose ends is not in the text. eastasia-06 could place the Tang court because its genre is a register of arrivals at it; this lemma is a country description and does not name the destination.
